text:
Once a Trap-Barrier System (TBS) is installed, it needs to be checked every single day, morning and afternoon, from setup until the trap crop is harvested, to stay effective.

Morning check: inspect each cage for rats or other animals caught overnight. Remove any catch from the cage. To dispatch a caught rat, this source describes submerging the cage briefly in water until the rat drowns. Also inspect the barrier and cages themselves for any damage (holes, tears, gaps) caused by rats or weather, and repair damage the same day if possible so rats cannot get through while the field waits for the next check. Clear debris out of the drainage channel so it doesn't create an easy path or hiding spot for rats trying to reach the barrier.

Afternoon check: return any emptied cages to their original position, secure them, and re-cover them with leaves/vegetation as before. Cages that consistently catch nothing can be relocated to a more active spot along the barrier.

Material care between seasons: rinse cages clean and let them dry in the sun before storing or reusing them - this reduces rat wariness toward a dirty cage and helps the material last longer. Repair cages carefully so they stay sturdy for the next use, and avoid leaving them out in the rain when not in use, since that shortens their working life. When removing materials from the plot at the end of a season, handle them carefully to avoid unnecessary damage, then clean and store them somewhere that avoids direct sun and other damage until the next planting cycle.
